stories.headline: Another bad Man United run has Carrick feeling the heat. Should he?
stories.summary: Michael Carrick is hardly unique in that he brought hope to Man United, but is he on course to become the latest coach to be fired midseason?
stories.body:
For many supporters, the Manchester United cycle appears to be back in full swing. An uptick in form under Michael Carrick renewed hope that the club could finally be moving in the right direction toward the end of the 2025-26 campaign, but it's been followed by a difficult start to the new season and pressure is mounting on the head coach.

It was a similar story for José Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim. Moments of optimism -- some briefer than others -- and then a sharp downturn that led to an seemingly inevitable parting of ways.

United have sacked managers midway through each of their past two seasons -- Ten Hag in October 2024 and Amorim in January 2026. Take it back further and managers have been dismissed mid-season in four of the past eight completed campaigns. The scrutiny on Carrick -- who only signed a two-year contract as permanent head coach in May -- has increased with United winning just two of their first seven games in all competitions.

A last-minute equalizer to secure a 1-1 draw at Fulham before the international break prevented a run of three defeats in a row but Carrick -- and the club in general -- is under the spotlight again.

The international break has been dominated by Manchester City and their legal case with the Premier League. United could end up with millions in compensation, but the most immediate -- and welcome -- consequence of the verdict breaking is that the spotlight has been focused on the Etihad and not Old Trafford.

Will that remain the case after Saturday's visit of Tottenham Hotspur, another club in turmoil? Or do we have reason to doubt Carrick's position as manager?

Is history repeating?

There's certainly a familiar feel about it all. Ten Hag was sacked after United won four of their 13 games in all competitions to open the 2024-25 season. Amorim survived a start of two wins from seven, but was gone by January.

Solskjaer lasted 17 games in 2021-22 despite finishing second the season before. Mourinho also finished second in 2017-18, but was dismissed just 24 games into the 2018-19 campaign. It's evidence of how quickly things can unravel at Old Trafford.

Carrick won 12 of 17 games last season after being appointed caretaker boss in January, suffering just two defeats and recording impressive wins over Manchester City, Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool along the way. No Premier League manager won more points during the same period as United finished third to qualify for the UEFA Champions League.

But just like the achievements of Mourinho and Solskjaer, it's been quickly forgotten. The defeat to newly promoted Hull City on the opening weekend put Carrick on the back foot immediately. The performance against 10-man Manchester City was poor, and losing to Brighton & Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup after leading 2-0 after 10 minutes was damaging.

Carrick, however, insists his team have been on the wrong side of some fine margins. Everton scored a stoppage-time equalizer thanks to an unbelievable strike from Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Erling Haaland's winner for City was wrongly awarded. Fulham's goal was also a freak incident when the ball rebounded off Senne Lammens and hit Lisandro Martínez.

If Carrick's theory is correct, then a run of good results might not be that far away.

What do the stats say about United's form?

The short answer: It depends where you look. United's players have taken a lot of criticism for a perceived lack of effort. Fulham ran an extra 6.5km (four miles) at Craven Cottage and Carrick's team have also been out-run by Hull, Ipswich Town and Everton. After five Premier League games, United rank 20th of 20 teams for distance at high intensity, time at high intensity, number of sprints and amount of time sprinting.

When a team isn't winning, these are damning statistics, but there's no real correlation between running stats and results. Leeds United were second for total distance covered per match last season and finished 14th. Aston Villa ranked 16th and finished fourth.

The more important questions are whether a team is running in the right way and at the right times. With Carrick reluctant to criticize his players in public, only he will know if they're following his instructions or not working hard enough.

United have been successful according to other metrics this season. They're second for shots on target per match and accurate passes per match. They rank top for accurate crosses per match and number of touches in the opposition box. They've also hit the woodwork more than anyone else.

United are 12th in the table after five games, but rank fourth for expected goals (xG) and seventh for expected goals against. Just based on non-penalty xG difference, the stats say Carrick's team should be fourth behind Arsenal, Brentford and Manchester City.

Money troubles

Many fans were left frustrated by the summer transfer business and believe Carrick has been left short. United were outspent by traditional big six rivals Manchester City, Arsenal, Liverpool, Tottenham and Chelsea. City, Liverpool, Tottenham and Chelsea all spent at least £100 million on a single player.

Sources have told ESPN that United's pre-summer budget was around £120m. In the end, Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba were signed for a combined £155m, while around £45m was recouped in sales.

Financial figures released last week provide some insight into why funds were so limited. United paid off around £150m from a revolving credit facility between March and June, and also spent more than £60m to acquire land needed for their proposed new 100,000-seater stadium.

Club sources have told ESPN that, in terms of summer transfers, they "operated within our means." United say they didn't have the budget to push the boat out further, but there's no escaping the fact that money is tight because of £1 billion worth of debt piled on by the Glazer family since their leveraged takeover in 2005.

Money could play a part in Carrick's future. United need regular Champions League qualification to build up their finances, and club bosses will be keeping an eye on the trajectory of results in relation to a top-four finish.

Where do United go from here?

Carrick is under no illusions that United's start has not been good enough. He can only hope that the long international break allows an opportunity for a reset.

The worry is that, on paper, United's early games looked winnable. And once action returns in October, the next block of fixtures appears daunting.

It starts with an awkward game against winless Tottenham at Old Trafford. That's followed by three tough away games against Atlético Madrid, Leeds United and Como before AFC Bournemouth at home and Chelsea away on Oct. 31. If United haven't turned a corner by then, the Halloween nightmare headlines write themselves.

Club bosses have not shown any indication that Carrick's job is under threat, but as usual, they will be guided by results. The pressure will ramp up with each bad result and poor performance, although United are in no mood to sack another manager after paying out close to £45m in compensation to dismiss Ten Hag and Amorim in the past two years. The only way to change it is by winning games.

Stories have already started to circulate in the Italian media that Antonio Conte would be interested. Eddie Howe, who has vast Premier League experience with Bournemouth and Newcastle United, is also available. United are known admirers of Kieran McKenna -- out of work since leaving Ipswich in June -- after speaking to the Northern Irishman when Ten Hag's position was under threat in the summer of 2024.

Carrick will get time to turn things around. The question is: how long?

stories.headline: Max Verstappen says F1 paddock 'less stressful' without Christian Horner
stories.summary: Max Verstappen said the F1 paddock is "less stressful" following Christian Horner's exit from the sport because "it is not nice when you constantly have tension between people."
stories.body:
Max Verstappen said the F1 paddock is "less stressful" following Christian Horner's exit from the sport because "it is not nice when you constantly have tension between people."

Despite being sidelined by Red Bull more than a year ago, Horner's possible comeback remains one of the hottest topics in F1.

Horner, 52, has already declared "unfinished business" and recently spoke of his "dream" to lead Ferrari, forcing the Italian giants to declare "full confidence" in team principal Fred Vasseur.

Horner's sparring with counterpart Toto Wolff, and latterly Zak Brown, shaped F1 for much of the past decade as Mercedes, McLaren and Red Bull fought on the biggest stage.

However, Verstappen insisted a potential Horner comeback is not required to reignite a paddock once compared to a "Piranha Club" because of its ferocity.

In an interview with the Press Association, Verstappen said: "To be honest, I like to see that people get on. It is not nice when you constantly have tension between people.

"Of course, from the outside, people like it, but honestly between the teams, it is better when you have just a friendly relationship. It is not as spicy, but I obviously quite like how things are going at the moment, with everyone's behaviour, let's put it like that.

"It is less stressful. We are all leading a stressful life and, when you can take a bit of stress out of it at times, it is good.

"He has shown he did a good job. Of course, people spread a lot of rumours [about Horner's future], and I don't know how much of that is true.

- Bahrain GP was the worst indictment of F1's new engine regs yet

- Could Malaysia return to F1 calendar? The state of play despite Sepang travel chaos

"I don't want to sound rude, but it is also not my problem or concern. He wants to come back, and if there is a good opportunity, I am sure he will do it, but I don't know where that is going to be."

Verstappen put aside his disdain for the sport's regulations to sign a new contract with Red Bull and commit his future to the sport for another four years.

The 72nd win of his career, in Malaysia -- which leaves him behind only Lewis Hamilton (106) and Michael Schumacher (91) -- arrived just days after Fernando Alonso signed a new Aston Martin deal to extend his stay in F1 beyond his 46th birthday.

"Staying here until then would mean I have dedicated more than half of my life to Formula One, and that is probably a bit too much," the 29-year-old Verstappen said. "I have extended for a few more years, and then I will look again and say to myself, 'Can I commit 100 percent?' And if not, or [if] there are other fun things around that deserves more time, then maybe I don't continue. I also want to spend more time at home and see the kids growing up."

Verstappen spoke with other teams -- including McLaren -- before re-signing with Red Bull. But would he be tempted to follow in the footsteps of Schumacher and Hamilton and drive for Ferrari? The tifosi unusually sang Verstappen's name beneath the podium following the Italian Grand Prix last month.

"I only want to win," he said. "I am not a nostalgic type. Do I have a lot of respect for the [Ferrari] brand? Absolutely. But if that means you then commit yourself, and you are driving P5 or P6, what's the point?

"I am very performance-driven, and I have won a lot with this team already. It is a second family at Red Bull, and the challenge of rebuilding is what's driving me."

stories.headline: Basketball Power Index: NBA projections, playoff chances for 2026-27 season
stories.summary: ESPN's Basketball Power Index projections for the 2026-27 NBA season are out, including a ranking of all 30 teams.
stories.body:
The NBA season starts Tuesday, Oct. 20, and ESPN has multiple previews to guide readers, including a ranking of the top 100 players, a look at the top players in new places and capsules on each team, with the most important stats that affect teams' win-loss records.

Now it's time for a season preview using ESPN's Basketball Power Index (BPI), which evaluates two different strength measures for all 30 NBA teams: one based on players currently available, and the other based on players who should be available during the playoffs. Then, to create preseason projections, the BPI takes into account win totals from the betting market in conjunction with each team's schedule and other factors, simulating the season thousands of times, with the results forming these projections.

Once the season begins, the BPI watches what happens in games and updates both its current BPI and its playoff BPI. There are numerous benefits to this, particularly that it adjusts game predictions on the fly when there are reports of players missing games. If Giannis Antetokounmpo is going to miss a game, for instance, the BPI marks down the Miami Heat's chance to win that game by an amount suggested by history. Sometimes, those injury reports are late or inaccurate (ahem, Joel Embiid) and it annoys us, the BPI and the league as a whole. But don't hold that against the BPI's model.

One thing the BPI isn't seeing this season is a secret prediction edge over Las Vegas. There aren't major deviations in this model's rankings from what Vegas is forecasting.

Let's dig into the projections, including how it ranks teams from 1 to 30 and which teams have the best chance to win the NBA Finals.

Jump to a section:

1-30 team rankings

NBA playoff projections

NBA Finals projections

More takeaways

Regular-season projections

The BPI values shown are the current numbers, not the version for the playoffs. The Golden State Warriors are down at No. 20, reflecting the absence of Jimmy Butler III, who tore his ACL in January and could return around midseason. The Warriors would be No. 12 if they were at full strength.

There is only one other team with an injury causing significant deviations between their current and playoff power: Embiid and the Philadelphia 76ers. That's because we know from history Embiid is going to miss games -- he has played 41 games per season since he was drafted and has played just 96 over the past three seasons -- and he is a good enough player that it matters. With Embiid, the Sixers have the third-best playoff BPI, consistent with the expectation they are among the favorites to come out of the East.

There are a few things to note from the overall league rankings. First, the Denver Nuggets finished last season as the league's best offense, and the BPI isn't going to argue that they got worse. They've been in the top six on offense for seven years now. They're, of course, led by Nikola Jokic, who was the No. 1-ranked player in our top 100.

Second, the Oklahoma City Thunder are far and away the best-ranked defense at plus-5.7 to the second-place San Antonio Spurs at plus-4.2. The Thunder have been No. 1 on that side of the ball the past two seasons and just missed at No. 2 the season before.

Third, notice that the best teams are driven by defense (Thunder, Spurs, Detroit Pistons) and the worst teams are, well, likely driving their coaches wild with bad defense (Sacramento Kings, Milwaukee Bucks, New Orleans Pelicans). In most years, offense drives the greatest difference across teams, but not this season. The range between the best and worst offenses is 8.0 net points per game, but it's 10.4 on defense. This is merely a forecast and not a fact, but it's something to watch as the game continues to evolve.

NBA playoff projections

The BPI can occasionally be a little overconfident. The model believes six teams in the West have an 85% chance to make the playoffs. Those numbers imply that it's unlikely that even one of those slips out of the playoffs. I have my doubts.

That doubt comes from knowing there is a realistic chance that someone on those top six teams gets hurt and it matters. Maybe that's Jokic or Kevin Durant or Luka Doncic. Those stars are important, having all been in the top 10 in overall Net Points added last season. Plus, those teams don't have the bench of the Thunder, whose bench could have gotten a No. 7 or 8 seed by itself based on a reasonable interpretation of their talent. They seem more fragile than a 10% chance of missing the playoffs.

On the Eastern side of the ledger, the story isn't all that different, though the bottom few teams are a little messier. From No. 6 to No. 10, there is plenty of room for teams to make it or fall out of the playoffs, where the Charlotte Hornets and Washington Wizards are not even shown because we stopped at 10 teams.

Not mentioned in these season projections: The Boston Celtics have a 75% chance of having at least the same record as the rival Sixers. But, if they are to meet in the playoffs, that is where the healthy Embiid factor kicks in and the Sixers have a 52% chance to beat the Celtics in a series.

NBA Finals projections

The Thunder have about a 1-in-4 chance to win the title, per the BPI's projections. Here are some game scenarios about equal to a 25% chance to win, to give that a little perspective:

Being behind by eight points at halftime
Trailing by four points with about five minutes left to go
Down 2 with a minute to go, but without possession

These are exciting situations. No one is leaving the game then unless they were only there to watch a mascot make a reverse half-court shot. Having a 28% chance doesn't sound like much, but it is an interesting number. It makes the rest of the league feel like they have a good chance, but those Thunder fans are also feeling good.

The Sixers' 8% chance needs perspective, too. That 8% doesn't change much if they rise to the No. 1 seed, where they'd go up to about 12%, or if they drop to the No. 6 seed, where it remains about 8%. Because the East looks fairly even across the playoff teams, the depth of the Sixers' stars keeps them competitive in the playoffs (especially if Embiid is healthy), no matter which teams they play. But even Embiid doesn't significantly bring up their chances to win it all when the Thunder and Spurs are so strong.

More takeaways from ESPN's BPI projections
This is the first season of the new anti-tanking rules. The updated draft lottery format means that really bad teams actually have a lower chance to get the No. 1 pick compared to merely ordinary bad teams. We put the new lottery rules into the BPI's system and let it project what expected picks teams would get. The big news out of that is -- and this is a little depressing for fans of competitive balance -- the Thunder have the third-best odds of getting the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft. Fortunately, it's only at about 11%, but they have about a 75% chance of getting a top-10 pick.

ESPN Analytics built this cool simulation of the lottery if you like watching balls bounce around to determine the fate of a franchise. I did it once just as I was writing the previous paragraph, and it landed the Thunder the No. 3 pick. I had to remind myself this was just a simulation and not reality.

In general, the odds of landing the No. 1 pick are much more flat, due to the new rules and the forecast of how teams will do this season. The Kings, for example, are projected to be the worst team in the league and their chances to get the top pick are about 7%, which ranks seventh. The Dallas Mavericks are predicted to win 10 more games than the Kings and have an 8% chance at the No. 1 pick. The new lottery rules create incentive to pay attention in real time during the season to where teams are likely to end up.

Finally, just for fun, the BPI can predict the likelihood of winning and losing streaks. Two teams are at about 70% to have at least a 10-game winning streak -- the usual suspects in the Thunder and Spurs. Both had streaks that long last season, but so did the Pistons, Nuggets and Atlanta Hawks. Last season, though, was when tanking teams were happy to fall into someone else's winning streak. Three teams had 16-game losing streaks and that lack of competitiveness probably raised the number of double-digit win streaks, too.

Of course, the most surprising streak of the season was that of the New York Knicks, who won 13 straight in the playoffs. Beating good teams over and over again in a march to a title is a dream, a statistical marvel. As much as we'd like to believe in the data and the calculations of the BPI, the basketball season that is about to start has a lot of the human factor and reason to watch beyond the highlights. You don't need the predictions. Enjoy the ups and downs of a game. The BPI didn't need to predict ups and downs because they will happen. Doncic, Jokic, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jayson Tatum, LeBron James and many other stars will have amazing games. You don't have to predict them, but watch them when you can.

Roll out the basketballs and let's play.

stories.headline: Winnipeg Jets, Montreal Canadiens unveil NHL Heritage Classic sweaters
stories.summary: After taking a three-year break, the NHL Heritage Classic returns with the Canadiens and Jets meeting outdoors.
stories.body:
After taking a three-year break, the NHL Heritage Classic returns with the Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets meeting outdoors at Princess Auto Stadium in Manitoba, Canada, on Oct. 25 -- and both teams will be dressed to impress with new sweaters.

The Jets are wearing white throwback jerseys that harken back to the original incarnation of the franchise in the 1980s and 1990s. It's a callback to their 2016 Heritage Classic sweater, which was also white with the team's legacy crest. This time, the crest is "rendered in felt with chain-stitched detailing, and the back numbers carry the same two-layer felt treatment," according to Fanatics, the NHL's authentic on-ice outfitter, which worked with the league and both teams on their jersey designs.

The Montreal sweaters feature several elements from other uniforms in the team's history while adhering to the franchise's iconic "bleu, blanc et rouge" color scheme. The Canadiens' logo is slightly redrawn and features running-stitch detailing.

As an Easter egg for fans, the words "Les Habitants" appear in the back collar for the first time, a reference to the team's nickname. There's also a fleur-de-lis on the team's loop label to honor their home province of Quebec.

The Heritage Classic is the NHL's Canadian-exclusive outdoor game series, launched in 2003 with a game between the Canadiens and the Edmonton Oilers. This is the fifth outdoor game for the Canadiens (three Heritage Classic, one Winter Classic and the NHL 100 game). It's the third outdoor game for the Jets, all Heritage Classics.

stories.headline: Silva rises in P4P women's top 10, making most of golden opportunity
stories.summary: After winning UFC women's flyweight title, Silva rises in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
The women's flyweight division might be the most stacked weight class in the UFC, and Natalia Silva wears the gold.

Silva was too fast, too precise and too elusive for Wang Cong in the UFC 332 main event on Saturday, and as a result, the 29-year-old from Brazil captured the vacant 125-pound title. She moves up one position to No. 4 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

Silva is one of seven flyweights in the women's top 10. The division with the next most pound-for-pound elites is lightweight, with three fighters in the men's rankings.

The top two fighters on the women's list are Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the UFC title last month while healing shoulder and back injuries, and Zhang Weili, a two-time former strawweight titlist who last fought at flyweight, in an unsuccessful challenge of Shevchenko in November.

Aside from Silva, there are three other UFC flyweights in the top 10 (Alexa Grasso, Manon Fiorot and Erin Blanchfield), and the rankings also include PFL 125-pounder Dakota Ditcheva.

UFC women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison has been missing from these rankings for the past few months because, with no fights since June 2025, she is ineligible. But Harrison will return from neck surgery to defend her title against former two-division champion and consensus GOAT Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 on Nov. 14.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Oct. 7. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which Natalia Silva captured by beating Wang Cong at UFC 332. When Shevchenko is healed up, she'll be looking to take back the belt.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Previous ranking: 4

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her upcoming bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Natalia Silva; 5. Cris Cyborg; 6. Alexa Grasso; 7. Manon Fiorot; 8. Dakota Ditcheva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Silva; 4. Zhang; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Fiorot; 9. Blanchfield; 10. Suarez.

Dre Waters: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Fiorot; 10. Suarez.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Ditcheva.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (38) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch at UFC 331. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight on the White House lawn. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from a challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 40
Goals: 36
Assists: 17

Oct. 6: Argentina 3-0 Benin

It was an emotionally charged night in Buenos Aires as Messi played his final international match for Argentina, the team that he had led to World Cup glory and two Copa América titles as captain.

The friendly match at the Estadio Monumental was goalless at halftime, but just a few minutes after the break Messi's in-swinging corner from the left was rattled home on the volley by Nicolás Otamendi.

Then, on the hour mark, Messi spotted Nico Paz in space 25 yards from goal. He fed a square pass with the outside of his boot to the Como player, who curled in a classy finish.

But the night undoubtedly belonged to Messi, and he fired a penalty into the top corner to cap off his 208th and final senior appearance for his country with his 126th goal.

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami

Before heading to Argentina for his final international match, Messi gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: 'One of the greats': Roosters' Daniel Tupou retires
stories.summary: The Sydney Roosters will be without dependable winger Daniel Tupou next season, after he confirmed he will retire with immediate effect.
stories.body:
Trent Robinson says Daniel Tupou will be remembered as one of the Sydney Roosters' all-time greats, after the four-time premiership-winning winger announced his retirement from the NRL.

Tupou is ending his 15-year career on a high after helping the Roosters win Sunday's Grand Final against Newcastle.

The 35-year-old, who had been coy about his future all season, became just the sixth player in Roosters history to win four premierships with the club.

Across a 307-game, one-club career, the winger scored 198 tries, the third most of any player in premiership history behind Ken Irvine and Alex Johnston.

"When you look at what Daniel Tupou has achieved over 15 seasons, he will stand as one of the greats," Robinson said in a statement.

"But those numbers only tell part of the story of Toops and what he means to this club.

"Since he made his debut, he has represented what we want a Rooster to be.

"He has been incredibly consistent, selfless and dependable, and whenever there has been a big moment or a tough moment, he has been present.

"Toops revolutionised the aerial game at the Sydney Roosters and became the greatest high-ball specialist of all time."

Tupou's exit comes as the Roosters prepare for a big off-season exodus over the coming weeks.

Fellow winger Mark Nawaqanitawase and back-rower Angus Crichton are moving to rugby union, Daly Cherry-Evans is heading to Super League side Hull FC, and Connor Watson is joining St George Illawarra.

But none of them get close to having the impact the towering winger has had on the Roosters since his NRL debut in 2012.

As well as four premierships (2013, 2018, 2019, 2026), Tupou has won three World Club Challenges and played Test matches for both Tonga and Australia.

He was part of the Tongan side that defeated the Kangaroos in 2019, in one of the biggest upsets in international rugby league history.

Tupou played 10 times for NSW at State of Origin level between 2014 and 2022.

"We love Toops, we're incredibly proud of him, and his name will always hold a very special place in the history of the Sydney Roosters," Robinson said.

Tupou retires as the greatest try-scorer in Roosters history after surpassing Anthony Minichiello in 2023.

He has the second-most appearances for Easts, behind prop Jared Waerea-Hargreabes.

"To have played my whole NRL career at one club means a lot to me," Tupou said.

"The Roosters gave me my opportunity and this has become my home.

"To play more than 300 games, win four premierships and share those moments with so many great teammates is something I'll always be proud of."

NRL games/tries: 307/198

NSW State of Origin games/tries: 10/3

Tonga games/tries: 23/13

stories.headline: NFL rescinds Juszczyk's fine, says it misunderstood celebration
stories.summary: The NFL has rescinded the $14,926 fine it imposed on the 49ers' Kyle Juszczyk for what it thought was a distasteful celebration of chugging a beer.
stories.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The NFL has rescinded the $14,926 fine it imposed on the San Francisco 49ers' Kyle Juszczyk for what it thought was a distasteful celebration of chugging a beer.

The league said it was withdrawing the fine to Juszczyk, whose nickname is Juice, "because his celebration was simulating drinking a juice box, not a beer ... Mr. Juszczyk finally stated that the fine is hypocritical with the amount of Bud Light sponsorships surrounding the NFL."

The league initially fined Juszczyk on Sept. 23 for "engaging in offensive demonstrations." According to the NFL, Juszczyk violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1 when he did an "imitation of chugging a beer" two separate times during the Niners' victory over the Miami Dolphins in Week 2.

Juszczyk immediately pushed back against the fine on social media and then held a brief media session during which he took the time to place a jug labeled in big letters "Not Beer" and put one of his thigh pads, emblazoned with a juice box, on his locker as a backdrop for the interview.

When Juszczyk was informed of the fine by Kyle Shanahan, he said he thought his head coach "was just messing with me."

Last Thursday, Juszczyk said he had his appeal hearing on Tuesday and said, "it seemed like it went well." Juszczyk said he believed "things are going to work out OK."

Juszczyk went on to explain how the appeals process works.

"It's what I imagine a court hearing would be like," Juszczyk said. "They read your fine and give you the letter of the law. They let you speak and basically, you explain what happened on the play, what your responsibility was, what you were thinking. And then your agent gets a chance to say what he or she wants to say. The NFLPA gets a chance to chime in and say what they need to say and that's it. And then you wait and hear your response."

The case Juszczyk made to the league was the same one he made to media during that Sept. 24 session at his locker. Juszczyk has been doing a celebration where he mimics drinking juice for many years. He pointed out that he wears thigh pads with a juice box on them and that Niners fans chant "Juice" whenever he makes a big play.

Juszczyk said he added that even if his celebration had was supposed to be him drinking beer, he didn't believe a fine would be appropriate.

"Even if it was beer, I don't think that should be a problem with all the beer endorsements that we have in the NFL," Juszczyk said. "We have everything. So even if it was beer, which it wasn't, I still felt like it wasn't an infraction."

Juszczyk said he thought the NFL was "going to realize that they made a mistake." That apparently was the case as the league overturned the fine.

According to Juszczyk, the juice celebration and fine led to multiple brands reaching out to him for endorsement possibilities. One of those, OceanSpray, signed Juszczyk to a partnership and is giving away 14,926 bottles of juice as part of that announcement.

ESPN's Adam Schefter contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Tottenham's Mathys Tel equals France under-21 goalscoring record
stories.summary: Mathys Tel will be hoping to take his goal-scoring exploits with France Under-21s over the international break into Tottenham's fight to turn their Premier League season around.
stories.body:
Mathys Tel will be hoping to take his goal-scoring exploits with France Under-21s over the international break into Tottenham's fight to turn their Premier League season around.

Tel has yet to score for Spurs this season but hit a hat-trick in a 7-1 win over Switzerland in Orleans on Tuesday night as France, who had already qualified for the 2027 European U21 Championship, completed their group campaign unbeaten with eight victories.

With 17 goals, Tel, who also scored in two other games over the break, has equalled Odsonne Edouard's record for France U21s and could have put himself into contention for a senior call-up to Zinedine Zidane's squad for the Nations League games in November.

"My brother had been nagging me about it [the goals record] for months. In the end it was in the back of my mind," Tel told reporters, as quoted in L'Equipe.

"With qualification [achieved], there was a different kind of motivation that allowed me to give my best, so now I am very happy."

Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham slumped to the bottom of the table ahead of the international break, with a 3-2 home defeat by Aston Villa a third loss from their five opening Premier League games.

The boss welcomed former player and first-team coach Gus Poyet to the training ground on Tuesday and appeared in good spirits as the pair chatted on the sidelines in a video on the club's social media account.

Spurs travel to Manchester United on Saturday and have a few fitness concerns following the international break.
